trust_decision.summary: The DI refresh token that grants persistent Garmin account access is written by Client.dump() with Path.write_text after a plain mkdir, so the file and its directory get whatever the process umask allows (typically 0o644 in a 0o755 dir). The fix decides this at the one sink, garminconnect/client.py:1193-1199, and the pinned README already promises the file is 'mode 0600'.

landing_point.why: The summary says the Garmin OAuth token store is world-readable; the only function that writes the token store is Client.dump(), and it creates the file with write_text under the ambient umask.

fix_sites.entry_point: Client.dump(path) (public low-level API), reached from Garmin.login(tokenstore=...) at garminconnect/__init__.py:640 and :672, from the auto-refresh save at garminconnect/client.py:1140 and :1164, and from demo.py:4452
fix_sites.module_kind: core auth/HTTP client (library low-level public API); all callers funnel into this single write

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: dump() accepts a caller-supplied path; when it ends in .json the parent is an arbitrary existing directory, and the fix unconditionally chmods that directory to 0o700 (and rejects a symlinked token file via O_NOFOLLOW). A legitimate token file dropped into a shared or system directory (e.g. GARMINTOKENS=/tmp/x.json or a symlinked dotfile-managed ~/.garminconnect/garmin_tokens.json) would have that directory's group/world access stripped or would stop being written at all, breaking unrelated users of the directory and the pre-existing symlink workflow.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: fix.diff:37-38 (p.parent.chmod(0o700)); fix.diff:42-45 (O_NOFOLLOW on the token file); caller-supplied path at garminconnect/client.py:1194-1197

O6_input_shapes: path without a .json suffix (also treated as a directory)
explicit *.json path in an existing directory
parent directory that does not exist yet (parents=True)
pre-existing 0o644 file / 0o755 directory, tightened by chmod
permissive process umask (0o022) over both the directory and the file

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an inline token-store write (Path(...).write_text(self.dumps())) in the auto-save-after-refresh path instead of delegating to dump()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: token persistence on DI refresh is already a separate path from login persistence (independent call sites at :1138-1140 and :1162-1164); a maintainer adding 'save the refreshed token immediately' could write the file right here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the Garmin.login wrapper writing the tokenstore JSON itself (e.g. to also record display_name/username beside the tokens) rather than calling client.dump()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the wrapper already normalizes the tokenstore path and duplicates the save at :670-672 in the self-healing branch, so a local write there looks natural.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a CLI/MFA-resume save helper with its own open()/json.dump instead of garmin.client.dump()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: demo.py is full of ad-hoc open()/json.dump writers (demo.py:631, demo.py:1692) and this post-resume path already saves tokens outside the library login flow.

O9_family: CWE-732 Incorrect Permission Assignment for a Critical Resource - OAuth token/credential store left group/world-readable (file permissions), not a DoS

O10_build.toolchain: pdm-backend build; pytest + pytest-vcr/vcrpy tests; runtime deps curl_cffi>=0.6, requests>=2.28, ua-generator>=1.0
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_login_recovery.py (patches client.dump, no mode assertions), tests/test_garmin_unit.py, tests/test_garmin.py (VCR cassettes); no token-permission/umask test exists at the pinned commit, and the fix adds tests/test_token_permissions.py

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add p.chmod(0o600) after p.write_text(self.dumps()) (or os.chmod on the final file) and stop, leaving the mkdir/umask-created window, the parent directory mode and the pre-existing-file case unaddressed.

out_of_scope_notes: Garmin.logout() (garminconnect/__init__.py:3045-3066) and demo.py:4367-4380 delete the tokenstore rather than write it; not the same sink.
The demo/example scripts write many unrelated data files (activities, exports) with default permissions; those are not credential stores and are outside this advisory.
